description: Spawn authority. The allowed-spawn edges themselves live in policies/agent-registry.json (field may_spawn) so there is exactly one source of truth. This file adds the defaults, the escalation mechanism and the enforcement contract.

defaults.unknown_caller_rationale: The main session (a human-driven Claude Code session) is not an organizational role and keeps full delegation authority. Only agents defined in this OS are constrained.

escalation.mechanism: A role that needs work from a role it may not spawn requests it from a role that may, or asks the human. Agents must state the escalation explicitly in their output.
human_escalation_required_for: creating a role that does not exist in the registry
any spawn during an active production incident that the incident commander did not request

notes: Claude Code has no nested agent teams: a teammate cannot spawn another teammate. It can still spawn ordinary subagents, so depth inside a team member is governed by the platform's subagent nesting limit rather than being capped at one level. This hierarchy governs subagent spawning throughout.
The hook can only see the agent type requested and the caller's agent type. It cannot verify intent. It is a guardrail, not an authorization system.

sre escalates to engineering-director, which is its reporting line. During a declared incident the incident-commander directs the response, but that is a temporary command relationship for the duration of the incident, not a line of escalation. The two were previously stated differently in policies/role-hierarchy.json and agents/sre.md.
